content: The image shows soybean seeds in an opened pod. Seeds appear cracked, shriveled, dull, with some grayish coating. Let me compare with top candidates.

Neither Downy mildew (leaf symptoms) nor White Mold (fluffy white mycelium on stems) match the test image.

The test image clearly shows an opened soybean pod with seeds that are:
- Cracked and shriveled
- Dull in appearance
- Some covered with grayish mold/coating
- Variable in size and quality
- Some appear decomposed

This matches the Phomopsis seed decay description perfectly: "Seeds that are cracked, shriveled, dull, and covered with gray mold; seedlings grown from infected seeds may be blighted."

Purple Seed Stain was the other seed-focused candidate, but the reference shows distinct pink-to-purple discoloration from the hilum, which is absent here. The test image seeds are gray/brown and moldy, not purple-stained.
